messages.content: Contemplate on few lines of “Part four” (page 153) of this novel, “Majid: Wake up, Bibi. I am going to take both of you to the village. When Majeed came out of the house carrying Jamila, wrapped in a thin... quilt, a bewilderedRahima at his heels, the brilliant moonlight at first blinded him.” Even if Majeed was mostly depicted as a cunning and apathetic person throughout the narrative, do you find the same character traits in the mentioned lines? Was he trying to save Rahima and Jamila out of good-will (deontology) or his action was well-calculated (teleology)?Explain it. Include at least 10 single-word palindromes, each at least 5 characters long.

message.content:
No, the quoted lines do not make Majeed suddenly kind. The passage gives us a moment of physical movement, not a moral awakening. The same traits are not fully on display, but the emotional temperature is still cold. Majeed wakes the women and announces a destination—“I am going to take both of you to the village”—which sounds like a command, not a promise of safety. The detail that Jamila is “wrapped in a thin quilt” reads more like a practical way to carry her than an expression of tenderness. “Bewildered Rahima” is described as confused and subordinate, “at his heels,” while Majeed’s own feeling is absent. The “brilliant moonlight” blinding him “at first” can be read as ironic: the light momentarily weakens him, but it does not make him compassionate.

If the scene is a rescue, the motive shown is not deontological. A deontological act would be performed because it is a moral duty or a right thing to do, with the women’s safety as an end in itself. Here, the language is goal-directed and mechanical. Majeed does not speak of duty, protection, or concern; he announces that he is taking them to the village. That makes the action more teleological: a calculated movement toward a result. The result may be that they are moved somewhere, perhaps to a place where they can be used, sold, or controlled. Even if the immediate outcome avoids harm, the textual emphasis is on control, not goodwill.

So the lines do not fully redeem him. Apathy is visible in the absence of emotional engagement; cunning is less explicit, but the commanding, instrumental tone implies a calculated use of the women. His action reads as well-calculated, not as a moral rescue.

The ten required single-word palindromes, each at least five characters long, are level, radar, kayak, civic, madam, cacao, refer, tenet, seres, deified.
